reference: GNU Coreutils wc selected from the harness reference PATH; each expected status is checked against GNU before candidate output and fixture-tree parity are assessed.
coverage: Default counts and selected line, word, byte, character, and maximum-line fields on ASCII text, empty input, and a final line without newline.
UTF-8 character counts and display widths, including multibyte, combining, and wide characters.
Unicode whitespace and POSIXLY_CORRECT word separation.
Tabs, carriage returns, form feeds, and maximum display-line width.
Multiple named inputs, per-file rows, total sums, maximum width totals, and repeated stdin operands.
NUL-separated filename lists with a space in a name, an unterminated final name, and an empty list.
Bash builtin type and help metadata against the documented wc help entry.
exclusions: Only the harness-provided GNU wc version and C/C.UTF-8 locales are compared; other GNU versions, locales, and libc behavior are not qualified.
Read/write error injection, malformed UTF-8 matrices, very large inputs, and every GNU option combination are outside this compact suite.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Compare default output and selected fields on ordinary C-locale text, including repeated spaces, tabs, an empty file, and a final unterminated line.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C
printf 'one two  three\n\tfour\nno-final' > basic
: > empty
wc basic
wc -lwcmL basic
wc -c basic
wc empty

cases.purpose: Compare bytes, characters, words, line count, and display width for valid UTF-8 with a multibyte accented letter, a wide character, a combining sequence, and a tab.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
printf 'caf\303\251 \347\225\214 e\314\201 \360\237\230\200\tX\n' > utf8
wc -lwcmL utf8
wc -m utf8

cases.purpose: Check GNU's Unicode nonbreaking-space word behavior and its POSIXLY_CORRECT change while an ordinary Unicode em space remains a separator.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
printf 'a\302\240b c\342\200\203d\n' > spaces
wc -w spaces
export POSIXLY_CORRECT=1
wc -w spaces
unset POSIXLY_CORRECT
wc -w spaces

cases.purpose: Compare -L tab-stop expansion, wide-character display width, and line-width resets at carriage return and form feed.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
printf '\tabc\tX\r123456\fwide\347\225\214\n' > widths
wc -lL widths
wc -L widths

cases.purpose: Compare multi-file rows and totals for selected fields, including sum semantics and maximum-of-files semantics for -L.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C
printf 'a\nb' > first
printf 'one two\n' > 'second file'
: > empty
wc -lwcmL first 'second file' empty
wc -m first 'second file' empty

cases.purpose: Compare stdin counting, repeated '-' operands after stdin is consumed, and an empty pipeline input.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C
printf 'first line\nsecond' | wc -m - -
printf '' | wc -l -w -c

cases.purpose: Compare --files0-from with a filename containing spaces, an unterminated final NUL-list entry, and the documented successful empty-list behavior.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C
printf 'alpha\n' > first
printf 'two words\n' > 'file with space'
printf 'first\0file with space' > names
wc -m --files0-from=names
: > empty-list
wc -w --files0-from=empty-list

cases.purpose: Check GNU-compatible nonzero status and diagnostic behavior when a named input cannot be opened.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C
if wc -l missing; then exit 99; else rc=$?; fi
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Check the GNU wc invalid-option exit status and diagnostic policy; preserve any candidate status difference as a parity failure.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C
if wc -z; then exit 99; else rc=$?; fi
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Check that wc is exposed as a Bash builtin and that Bash help contains the documented wc summary; this is metadata coverage, not wc operation coverage.
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t wc)
[[ $kind == builtin ]] || exit 1
doc=$(help wc)
[[ $doc == *'Count lines / words / bytes / chars in FILEs (or stdin).'* ]] || exit 1
printf 'builtin\nhelp-doc-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Missing values, missing file lists and conflicting operands report status 1 and preserve private inputs.
cases.script:
printf 'file\0' > names
printf x > file
wc --files0-from

cases.purpose: Missing values, missing file lists and conflicting operands report status 1 and preserve private inputs.
cases.script:
printf 'file\0' > names
printf x > file
wc --files0-from=absent

cases.purpose: Missing values, missing file lists and conflicting operands report status 1 and preserve private inputs.
cases.script:
printf 'file\0' > names
printf x > file
wc --files0-from=names file

cases.purpose: Missing values, missing file lists and conflicting operands report status 1 and preserve private inputs.
cases.script:
printf 'file\0' > names
printf x > file
wc -?

cases.purpose: Capture a directory read failure, then count a valid stream in the same shell; compare status, partial output and recovery.
cases.script:
mkdir folder
rc=0; wc -l folder || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
printf 'a\nb' | wc -lwm

cases.purpose: Count embedded NUL and ordinary invalid or incomplete UTF-8 in C.UTF-8 against the installed wc.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
printf 'a\000b \303\251 \377x \342\202' > input
wc -lwcmL input
